answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a refundable deposit in a shared registry, the atlas, before trading. New identities start with zero trust and earn quartz-clear attestations only by completing small verifiable jobs for established peers, each signed and timestamped. A ferrous-hard rule caps how many newcomers one deposit may vouch for, so spinning up a thousand fakes costs a thousand deposits plus real work, and flooding stops paying.
